**Yardstick.** This module describes itself as TFHE *gate bootstrapping*, so Scope is judged against tfhe-rs's `boolean` API and TFHE-lib — the gate-level libraries — not against tfhe-rs as a whole. A user who wants encrypted integers (`FheUint32 + FheUint32`) wants tfhe-rs's `integer`/high-level layer; against that yardstick this module is a building block (programmable bootstrapping is public, `testPolynomial` takes multi-bit LUTs, but there is no shortint/integer arithmetic) and would rate below mvp. That layer is filed under Backlog as a scope extension, not counted as a gap in this module's main use case.

**Where we are ahead:** the only implementation here that is **byte-compatible with tfhe-rs** in both directions — tfhe-rs decrypts this module's ciphertexts and runs its own `ServerKey` on this module's bootstrap and key-switch keys, and the bootstrap and key switch are byte-identical to tfhe-rs's on the same inputs (`interop_test.zig`, `tools/tfhers`) — so a Zig client can talk to a tfhe-rs server. Exact integer NTT instead of a floating-point FFT (no rounding error in the evaluation path, deterministic output); constant time measured under ctgrind (every in-file count 0) rather than asserted; a fail-closed typed entropy seam; pure Zig with no C — zig-tfhe, the only other Zig TFHE, needs a C compiler and states no interop, anchor or constant-time property. **Where we are even:** the whole of the tfhe-rs `boolean` user flow as its docs describe it — key generation with tfhe-rs's three boolean parameter sets (128-bit, `2^-64`/`2^-165` failure), client-side encrypt/decrypt, trivial ciphertexts, NOT/AND/NAND/OR/NOR/XOR/XNOR/MUX with unbounded depth, user-defined parameters (`Params` is an open struct), and keys/ciphertexts to and from bytes — and TFHE-lib's gate set. **Where we are behind (→ Backlog):** speed — ≈ 0.25 s per gate, about 20× tfhe-rs and ≈ 6× zig-tfhe's own claimed figure on different hardware, with no multi-threaded batch evaluation; no public-key encryption (tfhe-rs `boolean::PublicKey`, zig-tfhe); our byte format is not tfhe-rs's bincode/versioned serialisation (same container order, different envelope); no compressed (seeded) server key; only `EncryptionKeyChoice::Small`. None of these blocks the client/server gate flow; the speed gap is the one a user will feel first.

## What this module is

A TFHE/FHEW-style **programmable gate bootstrapping** scheme: LWE/GLWE/GGSW
ciphertexts over the discretised torus `T = Z_{2^32}`, with a blind rotation
(CMux over a GGSW bootstrap key) that refreshes a ciphertext's noise through a
programmable LUT, and binary gates on encrypted bits built on it
(`boolean.zig`). Bootstrapping is the step that makes FHE *unbounded-depth*:
the sibling `bfv` is leveled (bounded multiplicative depth); TFHE resets noise
after every gate.

The parameter sets, the key and ciphertext layouts, the gate encoding and the
bootstrap order are tfhe-rs 1.8.1's boolean layer (`EncryptionKeyChoice::Small`:
ciphertexts under the small key, PBS then key switch). The two implementations
interoperate in both directions; see Anchoring.

## Scheme choice — TFHE gate bootstrapping vs BFV/BGV digit-extraction

| | TFHE/FHEW (chosen) | BFV/BGV bootstrap (Halevi–Shoup) |
|---|---|---|
| What it refreshes | one LWE ciphertext per bootstrap (a gate) | a full packed BFV ciphertext |
| Core machinery | blind rotation = CMux/external-product loop | slot-packing + homomorphic digit-extraction polynomials |
| Ring modulus | power-of-two `2^32` ⇒ **exact wrapping `u32`**; the NTT uses an auxiliary prime internally and is exact | NTT-prime RNS ring (already in `bfv`) |
| Size / verifiability | self-contained; ~one accumulator loop | very large; digit-extraction is hard to get right and to verify |
| Dedup with `bfv` | none — a different scheme family | would extend `bfv` |

## Dedup / std-gap

- **std** ships `ml_kem`/`ml_dsa` (lattice KEM/signatures) but **no FHE** of any
  kind — no gap overlap.
- **`bfv`** is *leveled* FHE (add/multiply to bounded depth, no bootstrap). A
  different scheme family; shares no code.
- **`paillier`** is additively homomorphic only. Unrelated.

## Layout and conventions (tfhe-rs's, recovered as a black box)

`tools/tfhers` drives tfhe-rs's public API (`core_crypto` and `boolean`) and
dumps its standard-domain containers; nothing below comes from tfhe-rs source.

| Object | Order |
|---|---|
| LWE | `a_0 … a_{dim−1}, b`, `b = ⟨a,s⟩ + μ + e` |
| GLWE | `k` mask polynomials, then the body `Σ a_j·s_j + μ + e` |
| GGSW | `ℓ` level matrices, **least significant level first**; each `k+1` GLWE rows, row `r < k` with `μ·q/B^level` added to mask `r` (phase `−μ·w·s_r`), row `k` to the body (phase `+μ·w`) |
| Bootstrap key | `n` GGSWs of the small-key bits under the GLWE key |
| Key-switch key | per big-key coordinate `j`: `ℓ_ks` LWEs under the small key, least significant level first, phase `s_ext[j]·q/B^level` |
| Big key | the GLWE key's polynomials concatenated; sample extraction reads coefficient 0 with the negacyclic sign flip |
| Boolean | `true = +q/8`, `false = −q/8`; a gate = linear combination + bootstrap with the constant test polynomial `q/8` + key switch |

**The decomposition's tie rule.** A raw digit equal to `B/2` may be written
`±B/2`; key switching subtracts `digit·row`, so the choice decides the output
bytes. tfhe-rs's `SignedDecomposer` was sampled 40 000 times over five
`(B, ℓ)` shapes with ties planted at every level; the rule in `gadget.zig`'s
file comment (round to `ℓ·log B` bits; read the state as negative when strictly
above half its range, the rounding bit counting; then carry a `B/2` digit iff
the next raw digit's top bit is set) matches every sample. The digits are in
`[−B/2, B/2]`, balanced in mean.

## Evaluation path

`PreparedBootstrapKey` holds the bootstrap key forward-transformed by
`ntt.Engine(N)`. An external product decomposes the `k+1` GLWE components
(`(k+1)·ℓ` digit polynomials), transforms each once, accumulates
`Σ_row D_row ⊙ G_row,c` pointwise for each of the `k+1` output components, and
inverts `k+1` times. Exact: digits are `|d| ≤ B/2`, so every coefficient is an
integer below `2^{preparedBoundLog2}` (`(k+1)·ℓ·N·(B/2)·2^32`, `2^53` for
`tfhers_default`), which `Params.validate` keeps below `2^61 < p/2`; the residue
determines it and the result mod `2^32` is exact. A differential test holds the
prepared path to the reference `externalProduct`/`bootstrap` bit for bit.

Measured (ReleaseFast, this host, `bench.zig`), `tfhers_default`: bootstrap-key
generation 2.1 s, key-switch key 0.1 s, preparation 0.45 s; AND 247 ms, MUX
491 ms. The key generation was 15 s + 5 s before its samplers read entropy a
polynomial at a time: through `entropy.SecureSource` every `fillFn` call is a
`getrandom(2)`. tfhe-rs's SIMD f64 FFT is about 20× faster per gate; closing
that is backlog, not a correctness question.

## Error sampling

`toy` keeps the uniform error (bounded, `σ = bound/√3`). The tfhe-rs sets use
centred Gaussians with tfhe-rs's widths (a fraction of `q`), sampled by
`noise.zig`: Box–Muller from two 64-bit draws, with a branch-free `ln`
(exponent from the bits, atanh series) and `cos(2π·)` (integer range
reduction, Taylor polynomial), rounded with the `1.5·2^52` constant. Tested
against `std.math`: `ln` within `4·10^-15` (relative where `|ln x| > 1`,
absolute below), `cos` within `10^-14` absolute; truncated at `8.57σ`
(`u₁ ≥ 2^-53`).
Every sampler consumes a fixed number of bytes; a sampler and its bulk form
draw the same bytes in the same order (tested).

## Verification

1. **tfhe-rs interop** (`interop_test.zig`, `tools/tfhers`) — see Anchoring.
   This is the external, byte-exact anchor the core used to lack.
2. **Cleartext blind-rotation oracle** (`clearBootstrap`): a NOISELESS
   re-implementation of what blind rotation must compute, pinning LUT
   construction + modulus switch + rotation indexing independently of the core.
3. **Differential tests**: prepared vs reference external product and
   bootstrap (bit for bit, arbitrary GLWE inputs); bulk vs per-sample samplers.
4. **Homomorphic properties**: every gate's truth table on encrypted and
   trivial inputs, a 4-bit ripple-carry adder 40 gates deep, an unlimited-depth
   bootstrap chain, a corrupted-bootstrap-key control, the noise budget.
5. **Deliberately broken positive controls**: sign-dropped sample extraction,
   dropped-level decomposition, wrong-sign rotation exponent — each gives the
   wrong answer, so the checks have teeth.

## Noise / failure-probability ledger

For the tfhe-rs sets the failure probability and the security level are
Zama's sizing: tfhe-rs's boolean parameter page states "the standard security
of 128 bits" and an error probability of at most `2^-64` for
`DEFAULT_PARAMETERS` (`2^-165` for `PARAMETERS_ERROR_PROB_2_POW_MINUS_165`).
This module reproduces the dimensions, gadgets, binary secret keys and the
Gaussian widths exactly (pinned against tfhe-rs's constants), and its
bootstrap output is byte-identical to tfhe-rs's on the same key and input, so
the noise that sizing assumes is the noise this module produces. The `toy`
ledger is in `params.zig` (`erfc ≈ 48`, correctness only, no security).

## Threats / caveats

- **Security level is borrowed, not derived.** No lattice estimate was run
  here; the claim is tfhe-rs's for its parameters. `toy` claims nothing and
  `Params` is an open struct — `validate` checks structure, not security.
- **Entropy seam is typed.** Key generation and encryption take `io: std.Io`
  and draw through `entropy.SecureSource` (fail-closed on
  `std.Io.randomSecure`). They do NOT take `std.Random`: with `a` and `e`
  predictable, `dim` ciphertexts recover the key by Gaussian elimination, and
  the evaluation key (published) is an encryption of that key. The
  `…ForTest` twins keep `std.Random` for KATs and are compile-time refused
  outside tests.
- **Constant time, measured at the source/compiler level.** Key sampling,
  both error samplers, the NTT (key products in key generation, encryption,
  decryption) and the decomposition have no secret-dependent branch or
  index (the cleartext oracle `clearBootstrap` is a test reference and does
  branch on its key-derived rotation): `ctgrind_harness.zig` drives keygen /
  encrypt / decrypt / bootstrap / noise under valgrind and every in-file count
  is 0 (pinned in `scripts/checks/ctgrind-expected.tsv`). That took two
  inline-asm barriers (`ntt.zig`'s mask, `noise.zig`'s select): LLVM had
  turned masked selects back into `jb`/`jbe`. Not claimed: operand-dependent
  latency of `divsd`/`sqrtsd`/`mul`, or a timing measurement.
- **No authentication.** A corrupted evaluation key or ciphertext decrypts to a
  bit, not an error. FHE hides data; it does not authenticate it.
- **Probabilistic correctness.** Bootstrapping correctness is average-case;
  there is no worst-case guarantee, intrinsically.
- **Codec.** The 24-byte header is this module's; tfhe-rs's own serialisation
  (bincode + versioning) is not reproduced, only its container order. Decoders
  check the parameter fingerprint and that secret-key words are bits; they do
  not authenticate.

## Backlog / deferred

Ranked by the 2026-10-05 re-survey. **Missing and it matters** (against the `boolean` yardstick):

1. **Speed**: ≈ 0.25 s per gate, ~20× behind tfhe-rs and behind zig-tfhe's claimed ≈ 40 ms. Candidates: a vectorised NTT, a 32-bit-friendly NTT prime pair, keeping the accumulator in the transform domain across CMux steps, and multi-threaded evaluation of independent gates (through `std.Io`). Medium–large. The gap a user notices first.
2. **Public-key encryption** (tfhe-rs `boolean::PublicKey`, also in zig-tfhe): lets a third party encrypt inputs without the client key — an LWE public key of encryptions of zero, plus the security bookkeeping for its size. Small–medium.
3. **tfhe-rs's own serialisation** (bincode + `tfhe-versionable`), so files, not only raw containers, can be exchanged with a tfhe-rs program. Today a bridge must re-wrap `codec.zig` payloads. Medium.
4. **Seeded (compressed) keys**: tfhe-rs ships keys whose masks are a CSPRNG seed, ~`(k+1)×` smaller (this module's `tfhers_default` server key is ~78 MB). Needs tfhe-rs's CSPRNG reproduced. Medium.
5. **`EncryptionKeyChoice::Big`** (ciphertexts under the big key, key switch before PBS: tfhe-rs's `DEFAULT_PARAMETERS_KS_PBS`). Small.

**Scope extension, not a gap in this module's main use case:**

- **Integer arithmetic** on top of programmable bootstrapping (tfhe-rs `shortint`/`integer`: multi-bit messages with carry space, radix/CRT decomposition, carry propagation, comparison) and multi-value / larger-precision LUTs — what most tfhe-rs users call. Large; would be judged against tfhe-rs's `integer` API, against which this module is currently below mvp.
- **A parameter-selection helper** driven by a lattice estimate, for sets tfhe-rs does not ship. Medium.

**Deliberately not doing here:** GPU/HPU backends, ZK proofs of encryption, C/WASM bindings (CONVENTIONS.md §2: pure Zig, no C).

**Done since the 2026-09-30 survey (2026-10-02):** tfhe-rs's real boolean parameter sets with a stated security level (was `toy` only), the gate layer (`boolean.zig`), byte encodings (`codec.zig`), and tfhe-rs interop in both directions; they landed after the 2026-09-30 verdict and are what this re-survey re-judged.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class B · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class B** — published cryptographic or algorithmic construction with published vectors.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — anchored to an independent implementation through its public API.

**What the tests actually contain.** `src/interop_test.zig` over `src/testdata/tfhers_vectors.bin`, written by `tools/tfhers` (Rust, tfhe-rs 1.8.1, BSD-3-Clause-Clear, run as a black box with deterministic seeds; regenerating the file is byte-identical), and `tools/tfhers`'s `check` run on this module's own output (`tools/tfhers/zig_checked.txt`):

| Direction | What | What is asserted |
|---|---|---|
| tfhe-rs → here | the three boolean parameter sets | `params.tfhers_*` field by field, Gaussian widths bit for bit |
| tfhe-rs → here | 2 000 `SignedDecomposer` outputs over 5 `(B, ℓ)` shapes, half with a planted tie | `gadget.decompose` digit for digit |
| tfhe-rs → here | small `k = 2` set: secret keys, standard bootstrap and key-switch keys, 32 ciphertexts, their PBS and key-switch outputs, 7 gates × 16 outputs | ciphertexts decrypt; `keySwitch` **byte-identical**; this module's bootstrap (prepared and reference) with tfhe-rs's key **byte-identical** to tfhe-rs's PBS; tfhe-rs's gate outputs decrypt correctly and this module's gates on tfhe-rs's keys compute the same function; `codec.zig` payloads = tfhe-rs's containers word for word |
| tfhe-rs → here | `DEFAULT_PARAMETERS`: secret keys, 8 ciphertexts, 7 gates × 2 outputs from tfhe-rs's own server key | all decrypt correctly here; this module's server key for tfhe-rs's secret keys evaluates every gate on tfhe-rs's ciphertexts correctly |
| here → tfhe-rs | small set and `DEFAULT_PARAMETERS`: this module's secret keys, bootstrap and key-switch keys, ciphertexts and gate outputs (`tools/tfhers/emit_zig.zig`) | tfhe-rs decrypts every ciphertext and gate output; tfhe-rs's `ServerKey`, built from this module's bootstrap key (converted to its Fourier domain) and key-switch key, evaluates 112 + 28 gates correctly (the tool panics otherwise; first run, 2026-10-02) |

**How it got there.** Before 2026-10-02 the module had only `toy` parameters and no external anchor (oracle SELF). The interop work recovered tfhe-rs's conventions from its outputs (no implementation read), changed this module's layouts and decomposition to match, and found no disagreement in the core itself: the first run of the bootstrap comparison was byte-identical.
